definition: Computer systems designed to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as language understanding, prediction, generation or decision support.
A branch of artificial intelligence in which models learn patterns from data to make predictions or produce outputs.
The practice of designing and refining instructions given to an AI model to obtain more useful, reliable or controlled outputs.
The use of software or systems to execute recurring tasks or workflows with reduced manual intervention.
Large Language Model, a model trained on large amounts of text and used for language generation, transformation and understanding.
The process of using a trained machine-learning model to generate a prediction or output from an input.
Application Programming Interface, a defined way for software systems to communicate and exchange data or request actions.
A unit of text or data processed by a language model. Tokenization determines how input and output are represented internally.
A numerical representation of data, often text, that captures semantic relationships so software can compare or retrieve related information.
Additional training of a pretrained model on a targeted dataset to adapt its behavior or performance for a specific task or domain.
